name: Motorcycle Weak Battery Cranking Failure
explanation_template: Starter solenoid clicks rapidly and headlights dim while engine fails to turn over, indicating low battery cranking amps.
recommended_action: Measure resting voltage with a multimeter (should be >= 12.6V). Recharge with a trickle charger or replace battery if voltage drops below 9.6V under load.
preventive_maintenance: Clean battery terminals and verify charging voltage every 3 months.

name: Motorcycle Stator or Regulator Suspect
explanation_template: The battery continues to deplete despite recent recharging, indicating a failure in the charging circuit.
recommended_action: Inspect charging system stator coil resistance and rectifier output.
preventive_maintenance: Test charging system output at 3,000 RPM annually.

name: Motorcycle Stator / Rectifier Failure
explanation_template: Low AC output from the stator coils combined with persistent battery drainage confirms a burnt stator or failed regulator-rectifier.
recommended_action: Check AC voltage across all three stator yellow wires (should exceed 50V AC at 4000 RPM). Replace damaged stator coil or rectifier unit.
preventive_maintenance: Ensure regulator-rectifier heatsink has adequate cooling airflow.

name: Motorcycle Spark Plug Fouling

conclusion.title: Carbon or Fuel Fouled Spark Plug

explanation_template: The engine cranks normally but fails to fire, and spark plug inspection reveals heavy black carbon or wet fuel coating.
recommended_action: Remove spark plug, clean electrode with a wire brush, check gap with feeler gauge (typically 0.7-0.8mm), or replace with specified NGK/Bosch plug.
preventive_maintenance: Inspect spark plug condition and gap every 5,000 km.

name: Motorcycle Restricted Air Filter

conclusion.title: Clogged or Dirty Air Filter Element

explanation_template: Reduced engine power accompanied by black exhaust smoke and physical air filter clogging indicates rich air-fuel mixture due to airflow starvation.
recommended_action: Remove air filter element. Clean with compressed air if foam/washable, or replace immediately if paper cartridge.
preventive_maintenance: Inspect and clean air filter every 4,000 km, especially in dusty riding conditions.

name: Motorcycle Carburetor Pilot Jet Clogging
explanation_template: Engine runs only with the choke engaged and dies as soon as the throttle is opened or choke released, indicating a blocked idle jet orifice.
recommended_action: Disassemble carburetor float bowl, remove pilot jet, and clean orifice with aerosol carburetor cleaner and compressed air (never use hard wire).
preventive_maintenance: Drain carburetor float bowl before storing motorcycle for more than 30 days.

name: Motorcycle Wet Clutch Slipping
explanation_template: Engine RPM increases sharply upon acceleration without corresponding increase in rear wheel speed, signifying clutch slippage.
recommended_action: Verify clutch lever freeplay before disassembling clutch pack.
preventive_maintenance: Use only JASO MA/MA2 certified motorcycle oil for wet clutches.

name: Motorcycle Clutch Cable Misadjusted
explanation_template: Clutch slip caused by lack of lever slack, keeping constant tension on the clutch release mechanism.
recommended_action: Adjust clutch cable barrel adjusters to provide 10-15mm of free play at the clutch lever tip.
preventive_maintenance: Lubricate clutch cable and check freeplay monthly.

name: Motorcycle Worn Friction Plates

conclusion.title: Worn Motorcycle Clutch Friction Plates & Springs

explanation_template: Persistent slippage despite proper cable freeplay indicates friction plate lining wear below service limit or fatigued clutch springs.
recommended_action: Remove clutch cover, measure friction plate thickness and spring free length with vernier calipers; replace plates and springs as a set.
preventive_maintenance: Avoid aggressive clutch slipping and launch starts.

name: Motorcycle Front Brake Pad Wear Limit

conclusion.title: Critically Worn Motorcycle Brake Friction Pads

explanation_template: Brake friction lining is at or below 2.0mm and metallic scraping is heard, meaning backing plates are contacting the brake rotor.
recommended_action: Do not ride motorcycle. Immediately replace front brake pads and inspect brake rotor for scoring or grooving.
preventive_maintenance: Visually inspect brake pad wear indicator grooves every 3,000 km.

name: Motorcycle Spongy Brake Lever Air in Lines

conclusion.title: Air Entrapment in Motorcycle Hydraulic Brake Line

explanation_template: Brake lever compresses excessively close to the handlebar grip despite adequate fluid in the master cylinder reservoir, indicating compressible air bubbles in lines.
recommended_action: Bleed hydraulic brake lines using fresh DOT 4 brake fluid until all air bubbles are expelled and lever feel is firm.
preventive_maintenance: Flush and replace brake fluid every 2 years or 20,000 km.

name: Motorcycle Drive Chain Excessive Slack

conclusion.title: Excessive Drive Chain Slack & Derailment Hazard

explanation_template: Drive chain slack measures >= 45mm and slaps against the swingarm, posing a severe risk of chain derailment and rear wheel lockup.
recommended_action: Loosen axle nut, adjust swingarm chain tensioner bolts symmetrically to achieve 25-30mm slack, and retorque rear axle.
preventive_maintenance: Clean, lubricate, and inspect drive chain tension every 500-800 km.

name: Motorcycle Worn Sprocket Teeth

conclusion.title: Worn Countershaft / Rear Sprocket and Stretched Chain

explanation_template: Sprocket teeth show shark-tooth hooking and the drive chain skips under hard throttle, indicating pitch elongation.
recommended_action: Replace front countershaft sprocket, rear wheel sprocket, and drive chain as a complete matched kit.
preventive_maintenance: Never replace chain without inspecting sprocket tooth wear profile.

name: Motorcycle Front Fork Seal Oil Leak

conclusion.title: Blown Front Fork Oil Seal & Loss of Damping

explanation_template: Visible oil coating on the chrome fork stanchions combined with excessive diving under braking indicates ruptured fork oil seals.
recommended_action: Disassemble front fork legs, clean stanchions, replace fork oil seals and dust caps, and refill with specified viscosity fork oil.
preventive_maintenance: Keep fork stanchions clean of dried bug splatter and road grit.

name: Motorcycle Steering Head Bearing Notchy

conclusion.title: Brinelled or Worn Steering Head Bearings

explanation_template: Handlebars have a distinct notch or indexing detent when turning through center position, making low-speed balance and countersteering hazardous.
recommended_action: Elevate front wheel, disassemble steering triple clamp, inspect bearing races for pitting, and replace with tapered roller bearings.
preventive_maintenance: Check steering stem play and regrease bearings every 15,000 km.

name: Motorcycle Air-Cooled Cylinder Fin Overheating
explanation_template: Air-cooled cylinder cooling fins are heavily packed with mud or road grime, preventing convection cooling and causing thermal overload.
recommended_action: Allow engine to cool completely. Gently wash away debris from cylinder head and barrel cooling fins using a soft brush and degreaser.
preventive_maintenance: Inspect and clean engine cooling fins after riding through mud or unpaved terrain.

name: Motorcycle Liquid Coolant Reservoir Empty

conclusion.title: Low Coolant Level in Liquid-Cooled Motorcycle

explanation_template: Engine temperature is high and radiator fan is operating continuously, but coolant expansion tank is empty, indicating coolant loss.
recommended_action: Wait for engine to cool. Top up radiator and expansion tank with 50/50 ethylene glycol coolant; check for hose seepage.
preventive_maintenance: Check coolant reservoir level before long rides.

name: Motorcycle Petcock / Vacuum Fuel Valve Blocked

conclusion.title: Defective Vacuum Petcock or Blocked Fuel Screen

explanation_template: Motorcycle runs briefly on fuel in the carburetor float bowl then starves, pointing to a failed petcock vacuum diaphragm or clogged tank filter screen.
recommended_action: Inspect vacuum line to petcock for cracks. Disconnect fuel line into a container to verify steady gravity fuel flow on PRI or cranking.
preventive_maintenance: Flush fuel tank sediment and clean in-tank petcock mesh filter every 2 years.

name: Motorcycle Tyre Pressure Underinflated

conclusion.title: Low Motorcycle Tyre Pressure / Puncture Hazard

explanation_template: Heavy, wandering steering feel caused by low pneumatic pressure across front or rear motorcycle tyre.
recommended_action: Use an accurate pressure gauge to inflate tyres to manufacturer cold spec (typically 28-36 PSI front/rear). Inspect tread for nails.
preventive_maintenance: Verify cold tyre pressures weekly.

name: Motorcycle Tyre Exposed Cord Structural Rupture

conclusion.title: Extreme Tyre Carcass Failure / Visible Steel Cord

explanation_template: Steel cords or nylon carcass plies are visible through tread rubber. Catastrophic tyre blowout risk.
recommended_action: Do not ride the motorcycle under any circumstances. Transport motorcycle on a trailer to replace the tyre immediately.
preventive_maintenance: Replace motorcycle tyres before tread depth reaches 1.0mm or after 5 years from date of manufacture.
